questions.text: What distinguishes a cryptocurrency coin from a token?
options: Coins are mined, tokens are not.
Coins run on their own blockchain; tokens are built on a host blockchain and require the host's native coin for transfers.
Coins have a fixed supply, tokens do not.
Coins can be used for smart contracts, tokens cannot.
questions.explanation: Coins run on their own blockchains, while tokens are built on a host blockchain and their transfers must be paid for in the host's native coin.

questions.text: According to the transaction flow described, what step comes immediately after a transaction is signed with the private key?
options: The transaction is assembled into a block by validators.
The transaction is broadcast to the network.
The transaction waits in the mempool.
The transaction is confirmed on the ledger.
questions.explanation: The sequence runs: initiated in the wallet, signed with the private key, broadcast to the network, waiting in the mempool, assembled into a block, then confirmed.

questions.text: True or false: Sharing your crypto address with others is safe because it is derived from your public key and can be shared freely.
questions.explanation: True. A crypto address is derived from the public key and can be shared freely with anyone who needs to send you funds.

questions.text: True or false: If a scammer obtains your private key, they can sweep your funds without your permission.
questions.explanation: True. The private key is the master key that signs transactions; anyone who holds it controls every dollar in the account and can sweep funds without permission.
